processing_notes: Source states: 'SNNPR: During the reporting period, 287 of cholera cases have been reported from Zala and Uba Debratsehay Woredas of Gofa Zone, Miba and Marta Garda Woredas of Gamo Zone, Karati Zuria Woreda of Konso Zone, Male, Benatsemayi, Selamago and Hamar Woredas of South Omo Zone and Ale Special Woreda.' - interpreted as 287 sCh cases. Monthly (discrete-period) figure from the EDRMC Early Warning monthly bulletin, NOT a year-to-date cumulative. *** CONFLICT WITH EXISTING ROWS - FLAGGED FOR AGENT 5/7, NOT RESOLVED HERE *** This EDRMC figure of 287 cases for the WHOLE of SNNPR in January 2020 is SMALLER than the sum of four existing South Omo woreda rows for the same month: Index 17 Malle 364, Index 18 Selamago 228, Index 19 Benatsemay 188, Index 20 Hamer 74 = 854 cases, all dated 2020-01-01..2020-01-31 and sourced to 'UNICEF Ethiopia cholera response reports 2020' (metadata Index 5). Those four woredas are a SUBSET of the woreda list in this very sentence, so the parts exceed the whole by a factor of three. The most likely explanation is that the UNICEF/ECHO figures are cumulative over a longer outbreak window and were assigned a January-only TL/TR by an earlier agent. This row is entered because it is an explicit, dated, government monthly figure; Index 17-20 are left untouched because re-dating them requires returning to the UNICEF source, which is Agent 5's remit. DO NOT SUM this row with Index 17-20. NO WOREDA ROWS CREATED from this sentence: nine woredas across four zones plus Ale Special Woreda are named but no per-woreda counts are given.

source: Tahir Abdifatah, Compiled Body of Works in Field Epidemiology, Ethiopian FETP, Addis Ababa University School of Public Health, 2015 (AAU ETD) - Meher Need Assessment on Health and Nutrition, Jarar (Jerar) zone, Ethio-Somali Regional State, 26 November-12 December 2014
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 2011-12-12..2014-12-12. Source states: 'AWD: Birkood, Ararso, aware and Gashamo districts were not reported Acute Watery Diarrhea in the last three years while Degahbuur council, Guanaco and Degahbuur district had reported cases of AWD in 2004 [EC]. ... there was AWD occurrence in the last 3 years in 3 woredas (30%) of the zone ... Outbreak: There is no ongoing disease out breaks in Jerar zone in last six-month. [Meher season assessments were conducted from November 26 to December 12 /2014 in Jerar Zones ... 5 districts, 5 health center and 12 health post were visited during the assessment namely Degahbuur, Birkood, Ararso, Aware and Gashamo out of the 10 district of the Jerar zone]'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: partial. Birkood district, Jarar (Degehabur) zone, Ethio-Somali Regional State - one of the four of five visited districts explicitly reported as having had NO acute watery diarrhoea in the three years before the 26 Nov-12 Dec 2014 Meher assessment. INTERNAL CONSISTENCY CHECK that fixes the calendar: the same paragraph says AWD occurred 'in the last 3 years in 3 woredas (30%) of the zone', and exactly three woredas are then named (Degahbuur council, Gunagado, Degahbuur district) as having had AWD 'in 2004'. For that to be inside the last three years, 2004 must be ETHIOPIAN CALENDAR = 11 Sep 2011 to 10 Sep 2012 Gregorian. The bare '2004' is therefore EC, not GC. CONFIDENCE HELD LOW (0.65) AND SURVEILLANCE MARKED PARTIAL because: this is a district-health-office recall statement over three years, not a line list; the zone has no multi-sectoral coordination forum at district level and the zonal forum is 'functional only during epidemics'; and Somali is Ethiopia's highest-burden cholera region, so a three-year district zero deserves scepticism. Positive control that the system was detecting SOMETHING in the region in the same year: the same thesis documents a laboratory-investigated measles outbreak in Hamaro woreda, 43 suspected cases and one death, 6 April-5 May 2014, with five blood samples taken for confirmation. Sub-national row - does NOT assert national or regional absence.
